subtopics.title: Students engage in conversation, provide and obtain information, express feelings and emotions, and exchange opinions (1 of 5)

outcomes.text: Use appropriate gestures to convey and comprehend messages.
Respond to basic commands in classroom settings.
Ask and answer simple questions about basic personal information and the student’s immediate environment.
Exchange basic personal information orally, with emphasis on present time.
Initiate brief conversations applying basic language patterns, and familiar phrases and sentences.

subtopics.title: Students engage in conversation, provide and obtain information, express feelings and emotions, and exchange opinions (2 of 5)

outcomes.text: Use gestures and oral interactions to convey and comprehend simple messages.
Give and follow a short list of commands and directions in a variety of familiar situations.
Ask and answer questions to clarify information regarding routine and familiar activities.
Exchange information and ideas orally on everyday topics with emphasis on present, past, and future time.
Initiate and close short conversations applying familiar, recombined phrases and sentences and expressions.

subtopics.title: Students engage in conversation, provide and obtain information, express feelings and emotions, and exchange opinions (3 of 5)

outcomes.text: Use paraphrasing, circumlocution, and non-verbal behaviors to convey and comprehend messages in a level appropriate language.
Give and follow a series of commands and directions in a variety of familiar situations in public places.
Ask and answer factual questions on a variety of topics.
Engage in original and spontaneous communications on familiar topics with emphasis on a variety of time frames.
Initiate, sustain, and close conversations applying familiar vocabulary and structures to new situations.

subtopics.title: Students engage in conversation, provide and obtain information, express feelings and emotions, and exchange opinions (4 of 5)

outcomes.text: Use paraphrasing, circumlocution, and other creative means to express and comprehend ideas.
Give and follow a series of detailed instructions in unfamiliar or novel situations.
Ask and respond to factual and interpretive questions on a wide range of topics.
Exchange a variety of information orally on various topics related to contemporary and historical events and issues.
Sustain conversations applying new vocabulary and structures to common situations.

subtopics.title: Students engage in conversation, provide and obtain information, express feelings and emotions, and exchange opinions (5 of 5)

outcomes.text: Use culturally appropriate language and demonstrate culturally appropriate behavior in diverse settings.
Give, follow, and restate an extended series of detailed directions or instructions in unfamiliar or novel situations.
Predict answers to questions based on factual information on a variety of topics.
Express and exchange perspectives on a variety of topics supporting and defending opinions to convince others.
Engage in extended conversations applying new vocabulary and structures to common and new situations.

Respond appropriately to the tone and meaning in oral and written communications found in a variety of authentic sources dealing with a diversity of topics.

subtopics.title: Students understand and interpret written and spoken language on a variety of topics (4 of 4)

outcomes.text: Recognize and identify the location(s) and major geographical features of regions of the world where the language studied is or was spoken.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between the products and perspectives of the culture (2 of 5)

outcomes.text: Recognize and identify geographical features and analyze how geography shapes culture, perspective and language.
Interact in group cultural activities using appropriate patterns of behavior and courtesy expressions.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between the products and perspectives of the culture (3 of 5)

outcomes.text: Discuss how cultural traditions and their perspectives are shaped by geography and climate.
Engage appropriately in real or simulated cultural events.
Compare and contrast products, artifacts, dwellings and symbols, and their perspectives among same-language cultures.
Recognize, identify, place in chronological order, and describe the significance of important historical events in the culture(s) studied.
Recognize and identify artistic styles in the studied culture and discuss the meanings of examples of literary, visual, and performing arts from various historical periods in the culture(s) studied.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between the products and perspectives of the culture (4 of 5)

outcomes.text: Discuss and analyze how socio-economic, historical and geographical factors affect cultural practices and perspectives.
Discuss patterns of behavior typically associated with the culture(s) studied, and the perspectives associated with them.
Analyze and discuss how products and practices, such as political, educational and/ or economic systems, reflect both cultural and individual perspectives of the language studied.
Discuss and analyze how historical factors have affected some cultural practices and perspectives.
Analyze examples of literature, visual, performing arts, and other artifacts from the target culture(s) and discuss how they reflect individual, cultural and/or socio-political perspectives.

subtopics.title: Students demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between the products and perspectives of the culture (5 of 5)

outcomes.text: Examine what socio-economic, climatic, and/or geographical factors are affecting cultural practices and perspectives among the present societies where the language is spoken.
Discuss and analyze the evolution of patterns of behavior typically associated with the culture(s) studied.
Discuss and speculate about the international repercussions of historical events, political and/or economical structures, and value systems from the culture(s) studied.
Evaluate the impact historical factors have had or may have on the evolution and/ or preservation of some cultural practices and perspectives.

Evaluate the relevance of examples of literature, visual and performing arts, and other artifacts from the culture(s) studied and their impact on other artistic expressions(s) including those of the United States.
